topic: OmniScientist selected replay chronology, derivation boundary, and 36-case coverage binding
tested_scope: Public OmniScientist arXiv metadata/PDF, Omni-Scientist/omni-scientist.github.io Git history and replay artifacts, and public Omni-Scientist/OmniScientist release surface observed on 2026-08-29. This record does not claim non-public artifacts do not exist and does not transfer identity between repositories without an explicit bridge.

sources.observed: v1 submitted 2026-08-13 17:59:52 UTC; abstract reports evaluation on 36 real-data cases and completion in all 36.

Table 1 enumerates a 36-case suite; model section states Claude Sonnet 5 as the primary reasoning backbone and perception model; the run-output section states each complete run emits structured JSON, Markdown summary, replayable execution trace, and compiled PDF; appendix Tables 16/17 state statistics were recovered from stored traces of the 36 primary runs.

The root commit 7cee81bfbfa2fd7f9fe9aeaf07adacfcc8067848 has Git author/committer timestamp 2026-08-12T10:37:28Z and no parent; a later demos-changing commit e9808dcb2e648351257b2a7f4fa7ee82995b2c40 is dated 2026-08-24T13:07:21Z. Git timestamps are chronology evidence, not server-attested publication/receipt timestamps.
At the root commit the demos tree already contains birdaudio, galaxy_xsurvey, stead_seismic, and demos/index.json.
The public replay index contains exactly three selected runs: stead_seismic, galaxy_xsurvey, birdaudio.
The replay contains staged tool/action/results sufficient for strong selected-run observability.

The root replay presentation export declares log_full=false and contains explicit body-truncation markers such as 'trimmed for the web replay'; therefore this script is not a lossless canonical trace.

The selected replay log/script/paper artifacts changed across later site commits; current script packaging adds downloadable paper/log metadata. Replay export bytes are revision-scoped and should not be treated as immutable paper-time canonical bytes without a derivation chain.
Replay UI code describes figure field v only as a cache-busting token used when a redrawn figure keeps its filename. No observed generator semantics establish v as an execution timestamp.
Observed releases are later product releases (for example v0.2.0 published 2026-08-28) and did not provide an explicit paper-time evaluated-source/36-case replay bridge on the tested surface.

findings.summary: All three selected public replay directories are present at project-site root commit 7cee81b..., whose Git timestamp is about 31 hours before arXiv v1 submission. This strengthens replay-artifact chronology but is not a server-attested public-availability timestamp and does not identify the exact evaluated source/model/gate revision.

The paper says stored traces from all 36 primary runs were available for appendix trace recovery, while the public replay index exposes three selected runs. Public replay observability therefore covers a strict selected subset of the claimed evaluation trace population unless a 36-case archive/manifest bridge is supplied.

The root browser replay export is explicitly lossy (log_full=false plus trimmed bodies), and selected replay bytes later changed with site/export packaging. A browser replay must be bound to a canonical run by source trace digest, export-builder revision and transformation digest before it can authorize canonical-run evidence.

Replay figure v values are documented only as cache-busting tokens. Epoch-like numeric appearance is not sufficient evidence of execution/data/model time; timestamp authority requires explicit generator semantics bound to the canonical run.

OmniScientist's paper describes a four-artifact complete-run contract (structured JSON, Markdown, replayable trace, PDF). Public selected replay exports can be strong observability evidence, but suite-level or canonical-run provenance requires a derivation/coverage bridge to those canonical artifacts plus source/model/gate identity.

scope_limits: No claim that the three replay runs are or are not members of every paper evaluation subset beyond names/datasets visibly matching paper cases; exact run identity still needs a manifest bridge.
No claim that project-site Git author/committer timestamps prove when bytes became publicly reachable.
No claim that cache-busting v values encode execution timestamps.
No claim that absence of a 36-case public replay bundle on the tested surfaces proves no such bundle exists elsewhere.
protocol_implication: Separate presentation observability, canonical-run binding, and evaluated-suite binding. A selected or truncated replay may satisfy presentation observability, but canonical/suite authority requires exact source-trace derivation and suite coverage evidence.
